chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Hello there, in this video we are going to cover python functions.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And we have already seen quite a few.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For example the inbuilt functions that are very commonly used are len, print and input.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Len for example gives you the list of items inside of a container.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And while these inbuilt functions are useful, sometimes you want to have your own function

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: with custom functionality.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And this is what this video will be about.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: We are going to cover how to create a function that can do basically anything.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: You always have to start with the defined keyword.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: After that you will need the name for your function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: The naming scheme for this one is going to work basically identical compared to what

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: you have seen for variables.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Meaning you should be using generally a snake case and then not start with numbers, not

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: include random symbols, stuff like that.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: After that we need parentheses with the parameters.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Now the parameters might be a new word, but basically all they are, is a slot for the

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: arguments that we are going to add later when we are calling the function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: That's all this is.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: After that we will need a double colon, and then we can write whatever code we want inside

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: of the function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Also we can specify a return value.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Meaning once you are calling the function, you can either return a value, or you cannot

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: return anything.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: That's basically all you need for the basics of a function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Once again I am in VS Code and I want to create a new python file.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Let's call this one functions.py.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: After that back to fullscreen.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And now we can start writing any kind of function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For that we generally need two steps.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: The first one is the one I have just talked about, where we have to create a function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Let's create a really basic one.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For that I will need the keyword define, and then a function name.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And this function name obviously should reflect on the functionality of the, well, function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For now I simply want to create a function that print 5 times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: So we want to print a random message 5 times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: After that we will need parentheses, and for now they can remain empty.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Then a double colon, and now if I press enter, VS Code is going to give me one level of indentation

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: by default.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: In here I can now write any kind of code I want.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For now let me simply print test.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: This would be a valid function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Doesn't do anything useful, but at the very least it's not causing an error.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: This is the first step, where we have created a function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Next up, without the indentation, we have to call that function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And this is going to work in exactly the same way compared to what we have seen already,

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: for example with print, where we are calling the function with the parentheses.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And in there we can add any kind of argument, for example print for this one.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And the same thing we are going to do for our function, where we want to print something

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: 5 times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And this we also have to call.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For now we cannot add arguments, but if I run the code, you can see we get print, and

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: we get test.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Print is coming from this line, and test is coming from this line.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: But now in our case, we want to print this test 5 times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For that we will either need a while loop or a for loop.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: I am going to use a while loop, although both answers here would be perfectly fine.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: I want to once again create a counter, and this counter by default is 0.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Then I want to have a while loop, where we are checking if the counter is smaller or

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: equal than 5.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Inside of this while loop I want to print test, and then increase the counter by 1 on

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: every iteration of the loop.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And now if I run the code, we are getting test multiple times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: I suppose to make all of this a bit more descriptive, let's print the counter.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And there we get counter 1 to 5, and if I scroll up just a bit, we can see the 0 as

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: well and before that we have print.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And that's kind of all you have to know about functions at the very least to get started.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Essentially we are doing something very similar compared to the if, while or for statements

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: that we have seen in the last video, where we start with a keyword and then we write

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: indented code.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: The only difference now is that we have a function that we can call anywhere in the

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: code.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And this we can actually do multiple times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For example I could copy this line multiple times, and then we get the same output over

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: and over again.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Not terribly useful for this one, but certainly something you can do.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Although with functions we can customize things substantially.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Most importantly, when we have the parentheses at the creation of the function, in there

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: we can add parameters.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: These parameters later on would be the slots where we can add arguments.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For example I want to have the functionality that when I am calling the function, I can

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: add the word I want to print.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Let's call this one test for now.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: With that we have an argument for the function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: But this, if we are running the code, would cause an error, because print five times takes

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: zero positional arguments, but one was given.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: The function was given one argument down there, but it doesn't have a slot to capture this

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: argument.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For that we need the parameter.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: This we could call whatever we want.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For now let's simply call it parameter.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Doesn't really matter what you call it.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: If I run the code now, we get the outcome as before, but we cannot see the test anymore.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: That is because we have it available inside of this parameter, but we don't use it.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: The way this would work is that the parameter is now becoming a variable that is available

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: inside of this function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And only inside of this function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: You couldn't use it outside of it.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Which means, essentially what we can do.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Instead of the counter, I want to print the parameter.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And now if I run this again, we get test printed multiple times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And just to see a bit better what's going on, let me print the counter and the parameter.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: That way we get zero, test, up to five tests.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: We have added the string test to the function, which was captured by the parameter, which

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: then became a variable only available inside of this function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: The way we have used that is inside of the print statement, where we are simply printing

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: it.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: What you could also do is add a second parameter.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: In fact, you can have as many parameters as you want.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For example, what you could specify is, let's call it the loop amount.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Which is going to be the amount of times this while loop will run.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: To use that, we simply want to check if the counter is smaller than the loop amount.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: After we have that, we also have to give a second argument for this print five times

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Although the name now doesn't really work anymore, but that's an issue for later.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Let's say I want to print this test only two times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: If I now run the code, we get test three times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Because this one should actually be a smaller than, instead of a smaller than or equal to.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: If I now print it, we get test two times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: If I instead change this to a ten, then we are printing it from zero all the way to nine,

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: or ten times in total.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Also while we are here, let's rename this print five times to print x times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Both when we are creating the function and when we are calling it.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: That way the naming makes a bit more sense.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Another super useful thing that you can do, is to create a default parameter.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Let's say by default you want the loop amount to be 5.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Meaning if the user doesn't specify a custom number, let me remove it, we want this loop

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: to run five times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For that, you can simply add an equal to five or whatever default value you want inside

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: of the parameter when you create it.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: That way if I now run it, without the second argument, we are getting the loop five times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: You could also specify a default parameter, let's call this one loop.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: That way I can call the function without any arguments whatsoever and we get the loop five

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: However, if you do specify arguments, let's say some new numbers, I want to print something

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: and I want to print that four times.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: These values, if I specify them, are going to overwrite the default values.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: That way you don't lose any functionality by creating a default value.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Instead you basically create a backup variable.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: So if the user doesn't specify the value, you still have at the very least something.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: There are two more really important things that we have to cover before we finish the

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: basics of function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Number one is you can specify a return value.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For example, for this function, after it finished running, I want to return some kind of value.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For example, we could print out the loop amount, so we know how many times the while loop has

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: run.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For that you need the return keyword.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Anything right after that will be returned by the function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: In our case, we want to return the loop amount.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And that way, if you assign a value to a function after calling this function, let's call

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: this one test, and the value of this will be whatever we get from this function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And then on the next line, I want to print test.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: If I now run this, we are getting the value four.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: This is what that function returned, or more specifically what we have gotten from the

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: return statement.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: If I change this to, let's say the string something else, then the function is always

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: going to return this exact string.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Meaning if I run it now, we get something else.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: With that system, it becomes quite easy to get a function that returns some kind of value

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: after you call it.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Which makes it quite easy to connect it to some other parts of your code.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And this sometimes might become really necessary.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Because there is one thing for a function that can be very confusing and quite frustrating.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: When we have a function like this, you can't create variables inside of it, like the counter

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: I have created on the first line of the function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: However what is really important to understand, is that this variable is only available inside

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: of the function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: This is called the local scope of a function, which means whatever variable you create inside

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: of this scope, is only available inside of the scope.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: We wouldn't have access to it outside of it.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Which incidentally is called the global scope.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Meaning this is the local scope inside of a function, and then we have the global scope,

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: which is the general unindented line of any python document.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Also if you have multiple functions, you have a local scope for every function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Sounds a bit complicated, but basically what it means.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Imagine I want to print this counter somewhere else outside of the function in the code.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For example I want to print the counter after we are calling the function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: If I now run the code, we get name counter not defined.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Because this counter only exists within this function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: It doesn't exist outside of it, so python gets an error.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: What is however possible, is to have a function that looks at the global variable, so a variable

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: I created outside of the function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Let's call this one global var.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And for the value we can go with global variable.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: This global variable is available inside of the local scope of the function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: For example we could simply print global var.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: If I now run this, we get, if I go up a tiny bit, the global variable.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And this should make sense.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Global variables should be available everywhere.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: They should also be spelled correctly, that usually tends to be good practice.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: These variables are always available to any function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: So even in the local scope of a function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: However a local variable, like the counter, should only be available in the local scope

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: where it is needed.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: The reason for that system is that we have more modular code.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Imagine you have 10 functions, and all of them do some kind of counter thing.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: If you had the variable name available for all functions everywhere, then you couldn't

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: reuse this counter, you would always have to find a different kind of variable name.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Which might be doable with 14 lines of code, but imagine you have a program with 10.000

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: lines of code.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: You don't want to look through the code editor for every variable name.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Especially if you work with multiple people, this would be a nightmare.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: So global and local scope are really important to understand.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: But other than that, this is basically all there is to functions.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: They don't get that much more complicated.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: I suppose we could do one more example.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: If I exit the full screen.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Very early on we have written a Pythagoras theorem calculator, that looked like this.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: If you are watching this on YouTube, check a few videos back, this is where we created

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: this.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: So ultimately all we are doing is this formula.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Where we are getting the power of one side, the power of the other side, and we are putting

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: all of this inside of a square root.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: That way we are getting the hypotenuse of a triangle.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Within this python document we are doing all of this over 4 lines.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Which really isn't ideal.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: So instead, let me copy all of this, and instead create a, let's call it a hypotenuse calculator.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And inside of there we are going to paste in all of the code.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Now we have to make a couple of updates for all of this to work.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Also let me go back to full screen.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Now we can work with this.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Oh and a really nice feature inside of VS Code, is if you hover next to the function,

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: you can minimize it by clicking on the arrow.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Makes the code a lot more organized.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Ultimately all I want, is I simply want to call the hypotenuse calculator, then supply

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: two sides, and then the function is going to return the resulting value.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Ideally also rounded.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: All of this at the end I simply want to print.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: So let me print the hypotenuse, and add some basic values.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Let's say 5 and 10.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: We will need two parameters.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: One for side a, and another one for side b.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: With that we also don't need the input statement anymore.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: I actually want to get rid of both of these lines of code, because they are not needed

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: anymore.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: The only thing that we really need, is the hypotenuse.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And in there we still have the correct formula.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: This one can stay as it is.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: I suppose what we can do while being here, is standardize all of this.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: We should either use the power with two asterisks, or the power function.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Both would be fine, but we should only use one at a time.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Let's say I want to use the double asterisk, so side asterisk asterisk and 2.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Also this should be side b.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: That way all of this looks a bit more consistent.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: After we have that, we get the hypotenuse, and this is what we want to return.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: So return hypotenuse.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And then I can comment out all the stuff we have done before, so we can focus on one thing.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: If I now run all of this, we get some kind of value.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: To double check this one, let me change the numbers to 1 and 1.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: That way we know the value should be 1.41, and then a whole bunch of other values.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: So this seems correct.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Although I also want to round it, because these are way too many numbers.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: And rounding we can do right away when we are returning the value.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: All you have to do is wrap it inside of the round function, and then specify how many

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: numbers you want after the decimal point.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: In my case 2.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: If I now run this again, we get 1.41.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: With that I can use other values, let's say 5 and 4 do the same thing, and we get 6.4.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: That feels much cleaner.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Also what we could be doing for the hypotenuse calculator is define default values.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: I think 1 and 1 would be pretty good default values.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Finally, before we finish, there is one more thing that I do want to cover.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Sometimes you have a function with a huge amount of parameters, which can be quite confusing.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: In that case it might make sense to specify which argument corresponds to which parameter.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Which is called named arguments.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Basically all you do is you specify the parameter when you are calling the function, and then

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: assign it a value.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: In this case I want to have side a and side b, and then assign them a value.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: With that I can run this again, and we still get the same outcome.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: That looks pretty good.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: Now for this function this wouldn't be particularly useful, especially since we can exchange the

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: numbers and would still get the same outcome.

chunks.title: More on Functions
chunks.text: But imagine we have 20 parameters, then the system makes a whole bunch more sense.

chunks.title: More on Functions
